column1: # slug|impact,uniqueness,significance,experience,depth|category overrides or -|individual rationale
national-museum-of-korea|9.1,9.3,9.4,9.3,9.6|-|Exceptional national collection with substantial depth, but not as globally irreplaceable as the National Palace Museum's imperial objects.
changdeokgung-palace|9.3,9.4,9.6,9.4,9.2|-|Outstanding Joseon palace with preserved gardens, but visitor and historical scope remain below the Forbidden City ensemble.
bulguksa-temple|9.2,9.4,9.6,9.3,8.9|-|Silla architectural landmark with important Buddhist heritage; compact temple visitation differs from Angkor's vast complexes.
haeinsa-temple|9.1,9.6,9.7,9.0,8.7|-|Tripitaka Koreana gives exceptional textual heritage significance, not necessarily unrestricted visitor depth in its living monastery.
seokguram-grotto|9.0,9.4,9.5,8.9,7.7|-|Exceptional Buddhist sculptural chamber but short contained visit has far less depth than museum collections or large temple parks.
huwon-secret-garden|8.8,9.0,8.9,8.9,8.1|-|Unique royal garden tour within Changdeokgung; avoid inheriting all parent palace significance and discovery.
jongmyo-shrine|8.8,9.3,9.7,8.8,8.0|-|Confucian royal ritual significance is high; site experience and breadth are narrower than palaces or comprehensive heritage areas.
suwon-hwaseong-fortress|9.1,9.3,9.4,9.2,9.0|-|Important surviving fortification system, but the visitor scale is less globally singular than the Great Wall.
hahoe-folk-village|9.0,9.3,9.4,9.2,8.9|-|Living traditional settlement and heritage architecture, but globally comparable preserved villages exist.
yangdong-folk-village|8.9,9.2,9.3,9.1,8.7|-|Notable historic Korean clan settlement; distinguish wider village heritage from global reference towns.
jeju-island|9.2,9.2,9.1,9.3,9.6|-|Entire volcanic island offers varied experiences, but individual volcanic attractions carry their own scientific distinctiveness.
hallasan-national-park|9.2,9.3,9.0,9.1,9.4|-|Strong volcanic summit and high-altitude habitat, although comparable alpine national parks exist worldwide.
seoraksan-national-park|9.3,9.3,9.0,9.3,9.4|-|Outstanding granite peaks and valleys, but not every dimension merits rare worldwide benchmark status.
gyeongbokgung-palace|9.0,9.3,9.5,9.1,8.9|-|Major royal palace complex with deep history; avoid near-unique scale when compared with Forbidden City and Changdeokgung.
daereungwon-ancient-tombs|8.7,9.0,9.3,9.0,8.5|-|Important Silla royal burial mounds but interpretive depth and impact are below entire Gyeongju Historic Areas.
manjanggul-lava-tube|8.9,9.3,8.9,8.9,8.0|-|Excellent lava tube geology but a single cavern should not inherit Jeju Island's multi-site ecological depth.
ulleungdo-island|8.9,9.2,8.6,9.1,9.1|-|Remote volcanic island scenery and distinctive ecology, but not every experience dimension is globally elite.
geomunoreum-volcanic-cone|8.7,9.0,9.0,8.8,8.1|-|Important Jeju volcanic geology, yet focused volcanic cone trail is less substantial than the whole UNESCO volcanic ensemble.
jeonju-hanok-village|8.7,8.9,8.7,9.0,8.7|-|Attractive concentrated traditional streets with commercialized tourism; cultural atmosphere does not equate to top historic towns.
suncheon-bay-wetland-reserve|8.9,9.0,9.0,9.1,8.6|-|Outstanding tidal wetland and bird habitats, with visitor depth and global rarity below the largest protected ecosystems.
namhansanseong-fortress|8.8,9.0,9.1,8.9,8.6|-|Significant mountain fortress with hiking, but less monumental visitor distinctiveness than globally top defenses.
buseoksa-temple|9.0,9.2,9.2,9.0,8.5|-|Important wooden architecture and Buddhist landscape, but compact temple tour is narrower than grand temple precincts.
tongdosa-temple|9.0,9.2,9.3,9.1,8.7|-|Major Buddhist monastery with meaningful grounds, while global historical singularity is below top pilgrimage complexes.

gyeongju-historic-areas|9.5,9.6,9.8,9.5,9.8|-|Retain UNESCO historic ensemble spanning numerous archaeological monuments and 1000-year Silla urban culture; broad area is materially deeper than its individual tombs and temples. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/976

seongsan-ilchulbong|9.1,9.5,9.1,9.2,8.2|-|Keep exceptional UNESCO-listed oceanic tuff cone and global volcanological distinctiveness, while reducing exploration depth to the focused summit trail rather than all of Jeju Island. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1264/

bangucheon-stream-petroglyphs|8.9,9.5,9.6,8.5,8.5|history=9.8,culture=9.6|The 2025 UNESCO-listed Bangucheon property encompasses two major rock-engraving panels across a three-kilometre stream landscape documenting long prehistoric maritime and ritual art; this is a coherent historic ensemble, not a single etching. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1740

bangudae-petroglyphs|8.7,9.2,9.5,8.4,7.8|history=9.7,culture=9.5|The Bangudae rock art panel is archaeologically important for whale and animal imagery, but it is one component of the wider Bangucheon UNESCO property and usually a comparatively short viewpoint visit. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1740

bongjeongsa-temple|8.6,9.0,9.3,8.8,8.3|architecture=9.3,history=9.5|Bongjeongsa is a Sansa UNESCO mountain-monastery component with valuable historic wooden Buddhist architecture; the single monastery has narrower interpretive depth than entire Gyeongju Historic Areas. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

daeheungsa-temple|8.6,9.0,9.3,8.9,8.7|history=9.4,architecture=9.2|Daeheungsa's woodland Buddhist monastery forms part of the UNESCO Sansa serial inscription, with important monastic tradition but lower unique global monument density than Angkor or large historical capitals. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

beopjusa-temple|8.7,9.1,9.4,8.8,8.3|history=9.6,architecture=9.4|Beopjusa is an important Buddhist monastery in the UNESCO Sansa group, with monumental wooden pagoda and sacred landscape, while a single temple still has a concentrated sightseeing footprint. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

byeongsan-seowon-academy|8.5,9.1,9.3,8.7,8.1|history=9.4,architecture=9.3|Byeongsan Seowon contributes to UNESCO Korean Neo-Confucian academy heritage, combining education buildings and landscaped principles; its heritage significance exceeds the scale of one courtyard visit. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

dosan-seowon-academy|8.5,9.0,9.2,8.7,8.4|history=9.3|Dosan academy is a major Neo-Confucian educational site and UNESCO Seowon component, but lacks the combined depth and rare scale of the full serial academy group. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

gongsanseong-fortress|8.7,9.0,9.3,8.9,8.7|history=9.5,architecture=9.3|Gongsanseong is a substantial Baekje fortress and capital-defense ensemble inside the UNESCO Baekje Historic Areas; fortress walls and landscape allow meaningful exploration without duplicating the full heritage property. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

jisan-dong-tumuli-goryeong|8.5,9.0,9.3,8.5,8.2|history=9.4|The Jisan-dong tomb cluster is a significant archaeological element of UNESCO Gaya Tumuli with extensive elite burials, but mound visitation and museum interpretation have more modest immediate tourist impact. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

gochang-dolmen-site|8.6,9.1,9.5,8.3,8.1|history=9.6,culture=9.4|Gochang dolmens represent a major prehistoric megalithic group in Korea's UNESCO serial dolmen property; significant archaeology should not be equated with rich multi-room visitor experience. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

seonamsa-temple|8.5,9.0,9.3,8.8,8.5|architecture=9.3,history=9.4|Seonamsa is a historic forest monastery within the UNESCO Sansa group, notable for Korean Buddhist religious continuity and architecture, with site-local depth distinct from a whole national sacred landscape. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

tomb-of-king-muryeong|8.5,9.2,9.4,8.5,7.8|history=9.5,culture=9.3|The excavated King Muryeong tomb is central to the UNESCO Baekje Historic Areas and provides rare royal burial evidence, but its singular chamber has lower on-site exploration depth than entire fortress and museum ensembles. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/kr

jirisan-national-park|9.2,9.1,9.2,9.2,9.4|-|Jirisan was South Korea's first national park and spans an expansive mountain range with significant ecological and sacred-mountain traditions, providing much more than one summit viewpoint but less rare globally than the highest volcanic or glacial parks. Source: https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?menuSn=351&vcontsId=93604

hallyeohaesang-national-park|9.0,9.0,8.8,9.1,9.5|-|Korea's first marine national park spans six separate coastal districts and many islands, supporting varied multi-day sea scenery and hikes, unlike a single harbor overlook or beach. Source: https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/locIntrdn/rgnContentsView.do?vcontsId=110638

jinju-fortress|8.8,9.0,9.2,9.0,8.6|-|Jinju Fortress preserves major Imjin War battlefield history and accessible walls, pavilion and museum, giving deeper regional military history than a single monument but lower global military singularity than the Great Wall. Source: https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?menuSn=351&vcontsId=75199

gyeongju-national-museum|9.1,9.3,9.4,9.2,9.4|-|Gyeongju National Museum holds extensive Silla royal and Buddhist collections including national treasures and thousands of historical objects, with materially more museum depth than ordinary small local collections. Source: https://www.museum.go.kr/ENG/contents/E0608000000.do

mireuksa-temple-site|8.8,9.4,9.5,8.8,8.6|-|The excavated Mireuksa Temple Site forms part of UNESCO Baekje Historic Areas and preserves the enormous early Korean Buddhist pagoda, which justifies strong historical importance while its fragmentary ruins limit visitor immersion. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1477

donggung-palace-and-wolji-pond|8.8,9.0,9.0,9.3,8.0|-|Donggung and Wolji preserve the picturesque pond and secondary Silla palace grounds in Gyeongju, celebrated for night reflections, but a contained heritage pond visit should not inherit the city's entire ancient capital depth. Source: https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/locIntrdn/rgnContentsView.do?vcontsId=94404

jeju-haenyeo-museum|8.5,8.8,9.3,8.7,8.1|-|Jeju Haenyeo Museum interprets the island's UNESCO-recognized traditional women-diver culture through exhibits; intangible traditions merit significance, but this museum is distinct from experiencing the entire living coastal tradition. Source: https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=103315

hwaeomsa-temple|8.6,9.0,9.2,8.9,8.7|-|Hwaeomsa is a major Jirisan Buddhist temple with important pagodas and surviving wooden halls, meaningful monastic history but one temple rather than an entire sacred mountain. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hwaeomsa

baengnokdam-crater-lake|8.9,9.2,8.6,8.9,7.6|-|Baengnokdam is the summit crater lake inside Hallasan's volcanic caldera, an unusually memorable high-mountain view but much less independent depth than the whole national park.

daeseongdong-tombs|8.4,9.2,9.3,8.5,8.0|-|Daeseong-dong royal tumuli preserve Gaya elite burial history around Gimhae, nationally important archaeology but a focused mound landscape compared with entire Korean historic cities.

gotjawal-forest|8.8,9.1,8.8,9.0,9.0|-|Jeju Gotjawal contains unusual lava-rock forest soils, groundwater recharge habitats and endemic vegetation, a distinctive volcanic ecology with meaningful forest walking depth.

beomeosa-temple|8.4,8.8,9.0,8.8,8.6|-|Busan's Beomeosa has centuries of Buddhist history and impressive mountain-monastery halls, strong living culture but not globally as singular as the oldest preserved great sanctuaries.

independence-hall-of-korea|8.6,9.0,9.5,9.0,9.3|-|The Independence Hall of Korea is a large museum campus commemorating resistance to Japanese colonial rule, giving major historic significance and substantial multi-gallery visit depth. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independence_Hall_of_Korea

naganeupseong-folk-village|8.7,9.0,9.0,9.0,9.1|-|Naganeupseong preserves a lived-in Joseon walled settlement and traditional houses, with unusual town-scale cultural immersion rather than one reconstructed folk building.

marisan-tumuli-haman|8.4,9.1,9.3,8.5,8.0|-|Marisan tumuli at Haman record ancient Gaya royal burials and archaeological customs, serious national heritage but modest spectacle compared with large preserved palace ruins.

songgwangsa-temple|8.6,9.1,9.3,8.9,8.8|-|Songgwangsa is among Korea's major Seon Buddhist training temples with a substantial forest monastery, distinguished by living practice more than one monumental Buddha. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songgwangsa

woljeongsa-temple|8.5,8.9,9.0,8.9,8.6|-|Woljeongsa is a major Odaesan monastery noted for its octagonal stone pagoda and fir-lined approach, a fulfilling religious landscape but less globally influential than foundational Buddhist sites. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woljeongsa

juwangsan-national-park|8.8,9.0,8.4,9.0,9.2|-|Juwangsan combines dramatic cliffs, streams and autumn forest trails across a protected mountain landscape, varied scenery but globally comparable mid-altitude national park ecology.

oksan-seowon-academy|8.4,9.0,9.2,8.7,8.0|-|Oksan Seowon contributes to UNESCO Korean Neo-Confucian academy heritage through preserved wooden halls and scholarly history, one school less varied than the entire serial group.

ulsanbawi-rock|9.0,9.2,8.0,9.0,8.0|-|Ulsanbawi is an exceptionally dramatic granite ridge in Seoraksan reached by a demanding stair climb, high visual impact but not the full park's ecosystem or trail depth.

busosanseong-fortress|8.6,9.0,9.3,8.8,8.6|-|Busosanseong was a key Baekje capital fortress above Buyeo with riverside defensive walls and scattered remains, strong UNESCO historic context but below full Baekje heritage areas.

jusangjeolli-cliff|8.8,9.3,8.6,9.1,7.7|-|Jeju's Jusangjeolli has striking tightly packed hexagonal basalt columns meeting ocean surf, globally distinctive volcanic shoreline geometry but a confined coastal viewpoint.

seongeup-folk-village|8.4,8.8,8.7,8.8,8.6|-|Seongeup preserves traditional Jeju stone-wall homes and thatch-roof village architecture, authentic regional island heritage but not a large ancient capital. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seongeup_Folk_Village

jeju-olle-trail|8.8,8.8,8.2,9.2,9.7|-|Jeju Olle is a long interconnected island walking trail around diverse coasts, villages and volcanic landscapes, exceptional multi-day exploration depth without single-monument historic uniqueness. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeju_Olle_Trail

seoul-city-wall|8.7,8.9,9.1,9.0,9.1|-|Seoul's Joseon-era city wall survives as long hiking sections through mountains and gates, providing broad urban-fortification exploration though not the scale of China's Great Wall. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul_City_Wall

un-memorial-cemetery-busan|8.5,9.0,9.5,8.8,8.6|-|Busan UN Memorial Cemetery commemorates international soldiers killed in the Korean War and is globally consequential military remembrance, while the solemn cemetery visit is focused.

wanggung-ri-archaeological-site|8.5,9.0,9.3,8.5,8.4|-|Wanggung-ri retains Baekje royal-palace foundations and a significant five-story stone pagoda, important early Korean archaeology but less direct immersion than an intact palace. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaeological_Site_in_Wanggung-ri

hyangiram-hermitage|8.7,9.1,8.6,9.0,8.0|-|Hyangiram sits dramatically among cliffs overlooking the south sea with a longstanding Buddhist pilgrimage tradition, striking setting but a relatively concentrated hermitage.

jeju-april-third-peace-park|8.5,9.0,9.7,8.8,8.6|-|Jeju April 3 Peace Park commemorates the island's 1948 massacre victims through memorials and exhibitions, profound Korean historic significance with more depth than an outdoor monument. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeju_4.3_Peace_Park

jeongnimsa-temple-site|8.4,9.2,9.4,8.6,7.7|-|Jeongnimsa preserves a remarkable Baekje stone pagoda and excavated Buddhist sanctuary, central UNESCO heritage yet a smaller archaeological site than broad fortified capitals. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeongnimsa

cheonjeon-ri-petroglyphs|8.3,9.1,9.4,8.3,7.6|-|Cheonjeon-ri contains prehistoric and early historic engraved cliff images in the Bangucheon rock-art UNESCO heritage zone, irreplaceable artistic history but a short viewing stop.

sosu-seowon-academy|8.3,9.0,9.3,8.6,8.2|-|Sosu Seowon is Korea's pioneering Neo-Confucian private academy and a UNESCO serial-site component, stronger educational history than its compact grounds might suggest.

sanbangsan-mountain|8.8,9.0,8.4,8.8,8.0|-|Sanbangsan is a prominent Jeju volcanic lava dome with sea views and Buddhist grotto shrine, visually distinct yet smaller than the island's UNESCO volcanic ensemble. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanbangsan

yongmeori-coast|8.8,9.3,8.4,8.8,7.6|-|Yongmeori displays layered volcanic tuff cliffs and wave-cut coastal paths at the foot of Sanbangsan, unusual geological detail but tide-restricted brief walking depth.

may-18-national-cemetery|8.5,9.0,9.8,8.7,8.4|-|Gwangju May 18 National Cemetery commemorates victims of the 1980 democracy uprising, extraordinary national democratic significance, though a dedicated cemetery is focused rather than citywide.

oedo-botania|8.5,8.9,7.8,9.0,8.5|-|Oedo Botania is an elaborately planted botanical garden on a small island off Geoje, beautifully immersive but cultivated rather than a globally rare natural ecosystem.

bijarim-forest|8.5,9.0,8.8,9.0,8.6|-|Bijarim contains a large grove of ancient Japanese nutmeg trees in Jeju's volcanic landscape, biologically and atmospherically notable while still a limited forest circuit.

magoksa-temple|8.4,8.8,9.1,8.7,8.1|-|Magoksa is a UNESCO Sansa Korean mountain temple with historic timber architecture and monastic traditions, meaningful heritage with smaller visit depth than full pilgrimage landscapes. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magoksa

cheomseongdae-observatory|8.5,9.5,9.7,8.4,6.8|-|Gyeongju's seventh-century Cheomseongdae is one of the oldest surviving astronomical observatories in Asia, extraordinary science history but a tiny standalone stone tower visit.

ganghwa-dolmen-sites|8.5,9.1,9.3,8.3,8.0|-|Ganghwa Dolmen Sites preserve Bronze Age megalithic tombs as part of Korea's UNESCO serial property, important archaeology but exposed stones provide limited interpretive depth alone.

soswaewon-garden|8.5,9.0,8.9,8.9,8.1|-|Soswaewon is an intimate sixteenth-century Korean scholar's landscape garden with thoughtful pavilions and streams, culturally rich but not the scale of major imperial garden networks.

daecheongbong-peak|8.9,8.9,7.5,9.0,8.2|-|Daecheongbong is Seoraksan's high summit with substantial climbing routes and expansive mountains, a major demanding hike but narrower than Seoraksan National Park as a whole.
boriam-hermitage|8.5,8.8,8.1,8.9,7.5|-|Boriam is a small coastal mountain Buddhist hermitage overlooking Namhae's islands, exceptional scenery but much lower built heritage depth than major temples.

gamcheon-culture-village|8.6,8.8,8.4,8.9,8.8|-|Busan Gamcheon is a dense colorful hillside settlement with alley art, former refugee history and walking exploration, more socially layered than a simple painted mural wall. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamcheon_Culture_Village

gwangjang-market|8.7,8.8,8.5,9.2,9.0|-|Gwangjang is an old Seoul textile and street-food market with extensive vendors and traditional dishes, deep urban cultural activity but no world archaeological singularity. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwangjang_Market

haedong-yonggungsa-temple|8.7,8.9,8.4,9.0,8.0|-|Busan's Haedong Yonggungsa is unusually set on rocky sea cliffs with Buddhist shrines and ocean views, scenic visitor appeal above its comparatively reconstructed historic fabric. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haedong_Yonggungsa

cheongju-early-printing-museum|8.3,9.3,9.6,8.4,8.1|-|Cheongju's Early Printing Museum presents the UNESCO-recognized Jikji movable-metal printing heritage, exceptional global printing history but a focused museum not a vast collection. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheongju_Early_Printing_Museum
